nodes.label: Astro 5
nodes.rationale: Ships zero JavaScript by default, gives type-checked Markdown/YAML through Content Collections, and has i18n routing built in.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Pages Hosting
nodes.rationale: Free unmetered bandwidth on a global CDN, automatic SSL, deploy on git push. A VPS costs money and needs OS updates; shared hosting costs money and is slower. Total recurring cost is the domain, roughly RM50 a year.

nodes.label: Astro Content Collections
nodes.rationale: Schema-validated Markdown and YAML, so a malformed committee entry fails the build instead of silently rendering blank.

nodes.label: M12 — Deploy and Handover
nodes.rationale: Pushing to a parish-owned GitHub organisation rather than a student account is called the single most important line in the document: a graduating student's account is how the site is lost.

nodes.label: M3 — Content Collections
nodes.rationale: committee, gallery and schedule are language-neutral; roles are stored as keys and translated through ui.ts so a Bahasa Malaysia label can be renamed without touching the roster.

nodes.label: Browser-Only Editing Workflow
nodes.rationale: The guide is for the committee, not programmers: nothing is installed, everything happens on github.com. A wrong change is one click to revert, and a change that breaks the build is refused rather than published.

nodes.label: Schema Validation as the Test Suite
nodes.norm_label: schema validation as the test suite
nodes.rationale: A malformed committee entry must fail astro build rather than render an empty row, so zod schemas stand in for a conventional test suite on a site with no server logic.

nodes.label: Astro over Next.js or Nuxt
nodes.rationale: Next.js and Nuxt exist to run server-side logic and this site has none. Every page is known at build time, so a React or Vue runtime costs roughly 90 KB before a word renders and buys nothing.

nodes.label: Files over a Hosted CMS
nodes.rationale: Sanity, Contentful and Strapi tie content to a SaaS account owned by a student who graduates; when billing or the email bounces the content is gone. A git repository owned by the parish organisation does not expire.

nodes.label: Markdown and YAML over a Database
nodes.norm_label: markdown and yaml over a database
nodes.rationale: A database is for data you query, and nothing here is queried. Postgres or Firebase would add a service that can go down, expire or hit a free-tier limit in exchange for nothing. Files in git are also attributed and reversible.

nodes.label: Three Shaping Constraints
nodes.rationale: No budget (a student club cannot carry a monthly hosting bill), yearly handover (the committee turns over each academic year), and phones on campus wifi (most visitors arrive on mobile over a slow link).

nodes.label: Diamond Quadrant Layout (yellow / magenta / purple / lime)
nodes.norm_label: diamond quadrant layout (yellow / magenta / purple / lime)

nodes.label: Bilingual English / Bahasa Malaysia i18n
nodes.rationale: Astro's built-in i18n routing plus a plain string object covers it; an i18n library (i18next, vue-i18n) would be dead weight.

nodes.label: Language-Neutral Assets
nodes.rationale: Bulletin PDFs, gallery photos and committee names are stored once and shared by both locales; only the surrounding labels are translated. This is the single biggest saving in the build — sixty names typed once, not twice.

nodes.label: Header Language Switcher
nodes.rationale: Swaps the leading /en/ or /ms/ segment of the current path so it lands on the same page in the other language rather than bouncing to the home page. Two anchor tags, no JavaScript.

nodes.label: Pull Request Checklist
nodes.rationale: Encodes the four failure modes a non-developer contributor actually hits: one language updated, wrong bulletin filename, oversized photo, red build.

nodes.label: Content Authoring Checklist
nodes.rationale: The translation tracker: every row needs both locale files before launch, since the fallback renders English instead of failing.

nodes.label: M1 — i18n Core
nodes.rationale: The English fallback in useTranslations is deliberate: a missing Bahasa Malaysia string renders English rather than an empty element. Missing translations are tracked in the authoring checklist, not enforced by a crash.

nodes.label: prefixDefaultLocale URL Trade-off
nodes.rationale: URLs are /en/gallery rather than /gallery, accepted deliberately: in exchange every page is one file under src/pages/[lang]/ instead of a duplicated ms/ tree. Halving the files to maintain beats a three-character prefix on a site that changes hands every year.

nodes.label: First Friday Mass and Sacred Heart Devotion
nodes.norm_label: first friday mass and sacred heart devotion

nodes.label: Bulletin PDF Publishing Flow
nodes.rationale: The bulletin page globs public/bulletin/ at build time and sorts descending by filename. No CMS, no admin account, no upload form to secure, no server to store files on.

nodes.label: M4 — Home
nodes.rationale: "Today" is the build date on a static site, so events fall off only on the next deploy. Acceptable because Cloudflare rebuilds on every push and the bulletin is uploaded weekly — add a scheduled rebuild if it ever matters, do not add a server.

nodes.label: M5 — Main / Parish
nodes.rationale: One template covers Parish Priest, Deacon and Parish History across two locales. The bulletin index is the only logic: glob the PDFs, sort by basename, reverse, label the newest "This week".

nodes.label: Verification Drills
nodes.rationale: Bulletin drill, roster drill, Lighthouse on the heaviest album, a link sweep, a JavaScript-disabled pass, and a real phone on campus wifi. The final gate is handing the README to someone who did not build the site: if they get stuck, the README is wrong, not the person.

nodes.label: Bulletin Folder Filename Spec
nodes.rationale: Anything not named YYYY-MM-DD.pdf is ignored and reported in the build log, so a mis-named upload is visible rather than silent.

nodes.label: Central Latin Cross
nodes.rationale: Christ-centred: salvation and Christian faith at university as the foundation of the student community.

nodes.label: Logo Colour Palette and Liturgical Meanings
nodes.norm_label: logo colour palette and liturgical meanings
nodes.rationale: Gold for divine light and the papal colours, magenta for youth vitality, royal purple for Christ's sovereignty and liturgical solemnity, crimson for the Holy Spirit, white for purity, black for steadfastness.

nodes.label: CUTES Logo
nodes.rationale: A four-quadrant diamond badge on a cloud-filled sky, with the letters CU and ES split by a central cross so the acronym reads around Christ. Used as navbar mark, favicon source and hero emblem.

nodes.label: Holy Spirit Flame
nodes.rationale: Red/magenta flame on the left arm of the cross: Pentecost, spiritual fire, and the call for youth to be the light of the world.

nodes.label: Uplifted Hands
nodes.rationale: Praise, worship and service: youth lifting prayers and serving the church and campus community.

nodes.label: Theme Colour Tokens
nodes.rationale: gold #D4AF37, purple #7B1FA2, magenta #D81B60, crimson #E53935, ink #1A1A1A — sampled from the logo and defined once in src/styles/global.css.

nodes.label: Build Order Phases
nodes.rationale: M3 precedes M2 in Phase 1 so the layout renders against real typed data instead of placeholder markup that gets thrown away; the gallery is Phase 4 because it is heaviest and nothing depends on it.

nodes.rationale: No bespoke CSS architecture to hand over to next year's committee.

nodes.label: Bug Report Issue Form
nodes.rationale: Asks for page URL, device and screenshot in plain non-technical language so parishioners rather than developers can file a usable report.

nodes.label: Content Update Request Form
nodes.rationale: Exists for people who will not edit files themselves; the form steers self-service editors to CONTRIBUTING.md because that is faster than queueing behind a volunteer.

nodes.label: M2 — Layout and Chrome
nodes.rationale: Dropdowns are details/summary so the menu works with zero JavaScript; accessibility floor is a skip link, landmarks, visible focus rings, and gold used only at heading sizes where its contrast holds.

nodes.label: Parish Website Sitemap
nodes.rationale: The original brief: eight top-level sections (Home, Main, CUTES, BEC, Event, Gallery, Services, Resources, Contact). Every item in it is static content — no login, no payments, no accounts, no search.

nodes.label: Open Decision: What Is a Bulletin?
nodes.norm_label: open decision: what is a bulletin?
nodes.rationale: The requirements list a Bulletin section without defining it. Assuming a weekly PDF is why no CMS appears anywhere; if it is instead web text published by someone who will not touch git, Sveltia CMS is needed from day one.

nodes.label: Decisions Log
nodes.rationale: Settles the questions left open in TECH_STACK.md and forbids reopening them during the build: bulletin is a weekly PDF (no CMS), bilingual from day one (a missing translation is a launch blocker), full per-module specification.

nodes.label: Deferred, with the Trigger That Un-defers It
nodes.norm_label: deferred, with the trigger that un-defers it
nodes.rationale: Each deferral names the concrete event that reverses it (a CMS when the committee says the upload flow is too hard in those words; search past fifty pages; analytics when the committee has a question page views would answer). Each is cheap to add later and expensive to carry now.

nodes.label: Deliberately Not Included
nodes.rationale: WordPress, React/Next/Nuxt, any database, hosted CMS, an i18n library, a lightbox library, site search, a contact form and event registration are all excluded with a stated reason, so next year's committee can see what was skipped and why.

nodes.label: Git-based CMS (Sveltia / Decap), Deferred
nodes.rationale: The right answer if the GitHub upload flow proves too hard: it stores content as files in the same repo and adds only a login screen. Deliberately deferred, not rejected — add it when someone actually asks.

nodes.label: CUTES Committee Structure
nodes.rationale: Ministry of Leaders (Coordinator, two Vice Coordinators, Treasurer, Vice Treasurer, Secretary, Vice Secretary) plus seven ministries — Liturgy, Choir, Music, Multimedia and Publicity, Transportation, Recreation and Spiritual, Entrepreneurship — each with a Leader, an Assistant and open-ended members.

nodes.label: Committee Photos Are Optional
nodes.rationale: The roster must render correctly when every member lacks a photo: committee photos are the most likely thing never to be supplied, so the layout must not collapse without images.

nodes.label: When the Build Fails
nodes.rationale: A failed build keeps serving the previous working version, so nothing is broken for visitors; the error names the file and the field, and Revert is the escape hatch.

nodes.label: Most Holy Redeemer Church / CUTES Website
nodes.norm_label: most holy redeemer church / cutes website

nodes.label: Grouped Monthly Dependency Updates
nodes.rationale: Nobody remembers to update dependencies on a student-run site, so Dependabot does it; grouped into one monthly PR so the committee sees one thing to merge rather than fifteen.

nodes.label: BASE_PATH Sub-path Prefix
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages serves the repository from a sub-path, so every internal link must be prefixed. Read from the repository name so renaming the repo does not silently break every link.

nodes.label: Serialized Deploy Concurrency Group
nodes.rationale: One deploy at a time, queued rather than cancelled, so a bulletin uploaded a minute after a roster edit still gets published.

nodes.label: Pull Requests Build But Never Publish
nodes.norm_label: pull requests build but never publish
nodes.rationale: PRs run build and test only so a broken change cannot be merged without someone seeing a red cross, but never reach the live site.

nodes.label: localePath and assetPath Helpers
nodes.rationale: Never hand-write an internal href: the site is deployed both at / (Cloudflare) and /CUTES/ (GitHub Pages), so a hard-coded /en/... works on one and 404s on the other with no error in the build log. These are the only functions where a bug breaks every page at once, which is why they are the only unit-tested code.

nodes.label: Astro over WordPress
nodes.rationale: WordPress is how most church websites are built and how most of them die: paid PHP hosting, a database, and a patch treadmill. Skip updates for one semester after the student admin graduates and the parish domain serves a defaced page.

nodes.label: Filename-Ordered Gallery Photos
nodes.rationale: Photos render in filename order, so 01-, 02-, 03- prefixes are the whole ordering mechanism; no index file to keep in sync.

nodes.label: Gallery Albums
nodes.rationale: Mass, Fellowship, Sport, Retreat, Gawai Kaamatan CUTES, CUTES Family Day, After Mass, Chilling, Taize.
nodes.source_file: Requirement/MOST HOLY REDEEMER CHURCH, TANJUNG MALIM WEBSITE.md

nodes.label: astro:assets Image Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Automatic WebP conversion and responsive resizing at build time; the gallery is the only heavy part of the site.

nodes.label: Add Photos to the Gallery
nodes.rationale: Upload and commit; there is no list to update. A new album needs only a folder plus one entry in albums.yaml whose id matches the folder name.

nodes.label: M8 — Gallery
nodes.rationale: Photos live in src/assets so astro:assets processes them, never in public/. Built last on purpose: heaviest module, needs photos the committee must supply, and nothing else depends on it — if the launch slips, ship without it.

nodes.label: 2000px Photo Size Limit
nodes.rationale: Straight-from-the-phone photos turn a thirty-second build into ten minutes and will eventually make it fail, because every image is processed at build time.

nodes.label: Gallery Build Cost Warning
nodes.rationale: A folder of 4000px phone photos turns a thirty-second build into several minutes on Cloudflare's free tier, so source files must be downscaled to at most 2000px on the long edge before bulk uploads.

nodes.label: Static Map Image over an Embedded Iframe
nodes.norm_label: static map image over an embedded iframe
nodes.rationale: An iframe loads several hundred kilobytes of third-party JavaScript and sets cookies on a page that only needs to show an address; a photo plus a link does the job and keeps the page free of third-party requests.

nodes.label: mailto: over a Contact Form
nodes.rationale: A mailto link needs no server, no spam filtering and no form service. A form needs someone to watch an inbox that nobody will watch after handover.

nodes.label: Native <dialog> Lightbox over a Library
nodes.rationale: About fifteen lines of vanilla JavaScript on a native dialog element replaces a whole dependency; with JavaScript off, a thumbnail click opens the full image.
